text:
sophie: Hey folks — new hire here, trying to get the local dev stack running. Redis keeps losing data after I `docker-compose down` + `up`. Using `redis:7-alpine` and I tried mounting `./redis-data:/data` on my Mac (M1). Keys are gone after restart. Any obvious mistakes?

kai: Welcome! Quick Q: are you using a named volume or a host bind? Host binds on mac can be weird w/ permissions.

sophie: I did a host bind (`./redis-data:/data`). I thought redis persisted to /data by default.

omar: redis persists to disk only if appendonly is enabled or snapshots are configured. By default RDB snapshots happen but can be infrequent. If you want durable writes, enable AOF or configure save intervals.

jen: also check that the container can write to the mounted dir — on mac host-bind mounts can show up owned by root and redis can't write, so it falls back to memory.

sophie: ahhh that makes sense. How do I check? I tried `ls -la ./redis-data` and it shows root:root.

kai: either chown the dir to your uid or use a named docker volume. Named volumes avoid host FS permission quirks. Example compose snippet: 
```
services:
  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    volumes:
      - redis_data:/data
volumes:
  redis_data:
```

omar: if you want AOF and immediate durability, add a small config or command: `command: ["redis-server", "--appendonly", "yes"]` or mount a `redis.conf` with `appendonly yes` and `appendfsync everysec`.

jen: if you stick with host bind, do `sudo chown 1000:1000 ./redis-data` (or your uid) before `docker-compose up`. On mac the mapping is a bit different but it still helps in many cases.

sophie: tried the named volume approach — restarted with the `redis_data` volume and added the `command` to enable AOF. After a few restarts keys persisted. Thanks! :tada:

infra-bot: image redis:7-alpine pulled successfully (registry.redwood.internal)

kai: another tip — for local dev we usually keep `appendfsync everysec` (good enough) and avoid heavy persistence to keep iteration fast. For tests where you need a clean state, run `docker volume rm <project>_redis_data` or use ephemeral named volumes per test.

sophie: good call. One more thing — my app connects via `localhost:6379` but sometimes it times out after compose up for a few seconds. Any startup race recommendations?

omar: add a tiny retry/backoff in the app or use `depends_on` + a simple wait-for script. We also use `redwood-local-utils` script in repo that pings redis until ready.

jen: pinging is easiest. In compose, `healthcheck` can help too and `depends_on: condition: service_healthy` in v2.1+ if you care.

sophie: awesome — everything working now. Appreciate the quick help!
